paragraphs: All terrain robots exist because wheels stop at the first step. Legs, or legs with wheels on the ends, let a machine cross ground that was built for people, which is where inspection, security and delivery robots actually have to work.

The model holds 125,711 polygons and 132,806 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, and comes rigged for posing or animation. It is built to CheckMate specification, and native rigged builds for Cinema 4D and Maya are offered separately.
At $89 it suits robotics and technology visualisation, research and education material, advertising, science fiction film, game characters and editorial illustration. On sale since 2025.

An SPMT is a floor on wheels that can be joined to other floors. Every axle steers and lifts independently, so a load of any shape can be carried level across ground that is not, and modules are simply coupled together until the deck is big enough for a bridge span or a refinery vessel.

The model holds 725,389 polygons and 777,236 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, textured with 20 maps all at 4096x4096. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification, and a rigged build is offered separately.
At $89 it suits heavy transport and logistics visualisation, engineering and construction presentation, equipment marketing, documentary work and game environments. On sale since 2019.

Ordinary medieval clothing was cut from rectangles because cloth was expensive and waste was not tolerable. A tunic, hose and a belt is the whole wardrobe of most of the population, and its simplicity is historical rather than a modelling shortcut.
The set is light at 19,681 polygons and 14,032 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, suited to crowds and background characters, and carries StemCell certification.
At $89 it suits game characters and crowds, historical film and television, education and museum material, costume previsualisation and editorial illustration. On sale since 2025.

MIG welding put a spool of wire where a stick electrode used to be, which is why it took over workshops: the arc can run continuously and the operator does not stop every thirty seconds to fit a new rod. The cart exists because the gas bottle has to travel with the machine.
The model holds 109,819 polygons and 112,294 vertices in quads and tris with mixed UV layout, supplying the welder on its cart together with the helmet. It is built to CheckMate specification.
At $89 it suits workshop and manufacturing visualisation, tool and equipment marketing, training and safety material, film sets, game environments and editorial illustration. On sale since 2026.

The moustachioed businessman in a top hat and tails is a caricature that predates almost every company still using one. The handshake pose is the point of the figure: a mascot exists to greet, to close a deal, or to stand at the front of something being announced.
The character is light at 25,421 polygons and 25,709 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, supplied in the handshake pose. It is built to CheckMate specification.
At $89 it suits advertising and brand mascot work, board game and toy visualisation, editorial and financial illustration, animation and game characters. On sale since 2024.

Outdoor cooking is a logistics problem before it is a culinary one. Raw on one level, cooked on another, tools within reach and the fire in the middle: the multi level table exists because everything has to be somewhere and none of it can touch.
The model holds 138,968 polygons and 140,672 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, supplying the table together with the grill and tools. It is built to CheckMate specification.
At $89 it suits garden and outdoor living visualisation, product and retail imagery, hospitality and architectural scenes, advertising, film sets and game environments. On sale since 2026.

River boats in southern China were built to a shape settled centuries ago: shallow draught, a broad covered midships for passengers, and a sweep oar at the stern. They survived into the age of engines because the hull was already right for the water.

The model holds 61,629 polygons and 63,009 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, in aged condition, and carries StemCell certification. A second build of the boat is offered separately.
At $89 it suits cultural and historical visualisation, tourism and travel imagery, documentary and education work, film backgrounds, game environments and editorial illustration. On sale since 2022.

A polar bear is not white. The hair is hollow and colourless, the skin beneath it is black, and what looks like a white coat is light scattering through the fur. It is the largest land carnivore alive, and the one most often used as a symbol of something being lost.
The model is very light at 12,930 polygons and 13,197 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, textured with 3 maps all at 4096x4096. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification.
At $89 it suits wildlife and nature visualisation, climate and conservation material, documentary and education work, advertising, game environments and editorial illustration. On sale since 2016.

A portable launcher turns a drone into equipment rather than an aircraft. No runway, no crew, no airfield: a case that opens, a rail that fires, and an aeroplane in the air within a minute of somebody deciding they need one.
The model is light at 36,964 polygons and 38,359 vertices in quads and tris with mixed UV layout, supplying the launch system together with the UAV in flight. It is built to CheckMate specification.
At $89 it suits defence visualisation, documentary and news graphics, simulation, game environments and editorial illustration. On sale since 2026.

The XM250 is a belt fed weapon light enough for one soldier to carry and fire, which has been the goal of squad automatic weapon design since the machine gun was invented. Adding an optic to a weapon that fires in bursts is a newer idea and a surprisingly recent one.

The model holds 172,342 polygons and 173,493 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, supplied with the scope fitted, which is enough resolution for close inspection. It is built to CheckMate specification.
At $89 it suits defence visualisation and presentation, documentary and news graphics, game weapons, film props, simulation and editorial illustration. On sale since 2025.

Wheel alignment is measured in fractions of a degree, and the equipment exists because no human eye can judge it. Cameras on a stand read targets clamped to each wheel, and the whole rig has to be more accurate than the car it is measuring.

The model holds 321,610 polygons and 325,178 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, textured with 18 maps all at 4096x4096, in a generic scheme carrying no brand. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification.
At $89 it suits garage and workshop visualisation, automotive equipment marketing, training material, film sets, game environments and editorial illustration. On sale since 2019.

The design's whole argument is tolerance. Loose fitting parts that keep working when full of sand or mud, a stamped receiver that can be made anywhere, and controls simple enough to teach in an afternoon. Black polymer furniture is the modern production version of a very old pattern.
The model is supplied assembled, in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, and carries StemCell certification for use across engines and renderers.
At $79 it suits game weapons, film and television props, documentary and news graphics, defence visualisation, simulation and editorial illustration. On sale since 2025.

A catering trailer is a shop that arrives. The hatch opens into a serving counter, the black finish is a blank canvas for whatever the operator is selling this month, and the whole business model depends on the vehicle being easy to rebrand.
The model holds 115,214 polygons and 61,577 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, prepared as a mockup for applying artwork. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification.
At $79 it suits branding and livery mockups, food business and hospitality presentation, advertising, street and event scenes, film backgrounds and game environments. On sale since 2024.

Boxing gloves were introduced to protect hands rather than heads, which is why the sport arguably became more dangerous once they were mandatory. The shape has barely changed since: a closed fist, a thumb tucked away, and padding weighted by ounce rather than by size.

This is a collection listing rather than a single object, supplying the gloves as static pieces. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification, and three further volumes of the set are offered separately.
At $79 the set suits sports and equipment visualisation, retail and product imagery, advertising, broadcast graphics, game characters and editorial illustration. On sale since 2016.
